title: Howard Hughes: His Life And Madness

questions.q: What was Howard Hughes most successful at?
a: Designing, building and flying racing planes
Developing military planes and helicopters
Running a chain of hotels and casinos
Directing big-budget romantic comedies
questions.why: Lesson 1 says Hughes set speed and distance records with his racing planes.

questions.q: What does the summary say about his later aircraft projects?
a: They failed outside his circle of competence
They broke every record he attempted
They earned more than his aviation work
They were all sold to the government
questions.why: Lesson 1 says his military planes, flying boat and helicopters were unsuccessful.

questions.q: How did Hughes handle the Senate hearing?
a: He used the press and a test flight
He admitted the charges and paid a fine
He refused to attend and sent lawyers
He complained publicly about corruption
questions.why: Lesson 2 says he publicized Brewster's ties and demonstrated the H-4 during a break.

questions.q: Why did the hearing target Hughes?
a: A senator was allied with his airline rival
He had broken aviation safety rules
He owed taxes on his film studio
He refused to sell his TWA stock
questions.why: Lesson 2 says Senator Brewster was associated with Pan Am, a rival of TWA.

questions.q: What does his marriage and later life illustrate?
a: A single event cannot undo years of bad habits
Marriage can cure a drug addiction
Wealth solves most personal problems
A fresh start erases past mistakes
questions.why: Lesson 3 says the marriage and real estate could not repair his declining health.
